    problems
 4  To use various theoretical frameworks to understand health beliefs and predict health
     behaviours

     of India.

COURSE TITLE    COLONIALISM AND NATIONALISM IN INDIA
COURSE CODE     10PS0705
COURSE CREDITS  4

Objective:
 1  To provide students with a critical understanding of the various perspectives on
     colonialism, including liberalism, Marxism, and post-colonialism, and their influence on
     Indian nationalism.
 2  To enable students to explore and evaluate key approaches to the study of nationalism in
     India, including nationalist, imperialist, Marxist, and subaltern views, in a comparative
     context.
 3  To critically examine the political, social, and economic impacts of colonial rule on India,
     focusing on constitutional developments, the civilizing mission, and the effects on
     agriculture, industry, and ecology.
 4  To encourage students to engage with the role of social movements, including peasant,
      tribal, and women’s movements, in shaping nationalist politics and contributing to India’s
     struggle for independence.

 1  Students will develop a comprehensive understanding of the foundational perspectives on
     Indian nationalism.
 2  Students will demonstrate the ability to analyze the socio-economic impact of colonialism
     in India.
 3  Students will critically examine and differentiate the phases of India’s nationalist
    movements.
